correctness.rationale: The stationary angle is a Brownian convolution of ν with an independent exponential reset age, giving π_n=rν_n/(r+4n²D_rot). Conditional on the angular path the projected displacement is centered Gaussian with variance 2(d₀t+δA_φ). Right continuity and boundedness imply the short-time normalized even moment has highest coefficient (δ/2)^kπ_k before the nonzero Gaussian prefactor, proving necessity for every k. Independently of the frozen ODE, expand a j-fold time product of cosines and condition on the Poisson clock. Within each segment the initial angular law is π for the segment containing 0 and ν for later segments. Independence of its Brownian increments gives a factor π_b or ν_b at the segment's signed harmonic sum b. If j≤m all products with any nonzero b vanish; surviving products have zero total directional harmonic. This proves sufficiency at every time and agrees with the closed ODE's phase symmetry. Directional homogeneous polynomials determine the symmetric moment tensors; odd ones vanish. The Toeplitz identity has rank m+1, and the square factor at equality is unitary, forcing equal weights and a complete coset of (m+1)-th roots of unity in doubled-angle coordinates. For ν₁=0 the lagged cosine covariance is its stationary squared mean cosine factor E[cos²(2(θ−φ))] times exp(−ωs). The double integral gives Var(A_φ)=H(t)[1+Re(π₂e^(−4iφ))], and Gaussian variance mixing gives 12δ² times this variance as the fourth cumulant. For the regular three axes the t³ term's only nonconstant harmonic comes from δ³cos³, hence coefficient 120δ³/4 times the real third harmonic; opposite signs at the two stated directions double this. The short-time limit is uniform in direction by boundedness and the uniform Lipschitz bound on the cosine difference for a given change of θ.
residual_risks: The reported 103 checks are finite ODE and algebraic diagnostics, not interval certification or proof. Necessity refers to isotropy for every positive time, with stationary initialization; not to an arbitrary single selected time or to full-law isotropy from finitely many orders.
